name: Javier Sotomayor
milestone_by_age_26: Set world junior record at 2.33m at age 16 (May 1984) and first senior world record at 2.43m at age 20 (September 1988), becoming the first person to clear 8 feet in 1989.
early_history_summary: Sotomayor was sent to a Cuban sports school as a prospective basketball player due to his height, but coaches redirected him to high jump at age 14. He cleared 2 metres at 14 and set the world junior record at 16, reaching world No. 5 ranking by 19. He won Pan American Games gold in 1987 and set his first senior world record in 1988.
family_context_summary: Son of a day-care worker and a sugar factory maintenance man from Limonar, Matanzas Province, Cuba. Working-class family with no documented athletic background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents were not involved in athletics; Sotomayor was channeled into sport through the Cuban state sports school system.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban sports school, state athletic pipeline, early specialization, physical prodigy
evidence_summary: Sotomayor was identified by the Cuban state sports system as a teenager and channeled into high jump at 14, quickly setting world junior records by 16. His parents were working-class (day-care worker and sugar factory maintenance man) with no athletic background, so his advantage came from the elite Cuban sports pipeline rather than family resources. His exceptional physical ability — clearing 2m at 14 and 2.33m at 16 — marked him as a prodigy whose talent changed institutional response. The Cuban sports school system provided facilities, coaching, and competition access that would have been otherwise unavailable.

name: Vlade Divac
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Yugoslavia senior national team at the 1986 FIBA World Championship at age 18 and won gold at the 1987 FIBA Junior World Championship; was an established NBA player with the Lakers by age 24.
early_history_summary: Divac began playing basketball in his hometown of Prijepolje and moved to Kraljevo at age 14 to pursue a professional career. He debuted professionally with Sloga at 16, scoring 27 points against Crvena zvezda. He signed with KK Partizan in 1986 and immediately debuted for the senior Yugoslavia national team at the World Championship in Madrid.
family_context_summary: From Prijepolje, a small town in Serbia. Family background is not well documented in reviewed sources; he left home at 14 to pursue basketball in Kraljevo.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family basketball background or athletic inheritance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yugoslav basketball pipeline, elite coaching, exceptional peers, physical advantage, early pro debut
evidence_summary: Divac benefited from Yugoslavia's elite basketball scouting and development system, which identified him as a teenager and placed him on junior and senior national teams alongside future NBA players like Toni Kukoc and Drazen Petrovic. His 7'1" frame with coordinated passing skills was a rare physical advantage. He received individualized coaching from Krešimir Ćosić, the Yugoslav national team coach, and joined KK Partizan where he paired with point guard Aleksandar Djordjevic. His family background is poorly documented; no evidence of family basketball connections or financial advantage was found.

name: Shah Rukh Khan
milestone_by_age_26: Landed leading role in nationally broadcast TV series Fauji (1989) at age 23, followed by Circus (1989-90) and other TV roles, establishing him as a recognized television actor before his 1992 film debut.
early_history_summary: Khan grew up in Delhi and became involved in theatre during his college years at Hansraj College. His first starring role was in Lekh Tandon's TV series Dil Dariya (began shooting 1988), but production delays led to Fauji (1989) becoming his debut. He appeared in multiple TV series before moving to Mumbai in 1991 to pursue film acting.
family_context_summary: Born in New Delhi to a middle-class family. His father, Taj Mohammed Khan, was a businessman; his mother, Lateef Fatima Khan, was a social worker. His father died when SRK was around 15, and his mother died around 1991, creating significant financial and emotional hardship.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family connections to the entertainment industry; SRK entered acting through college theatre.
primary_early_advantage_tags: parental loss, financial hardship, Delhi theatre, television expansion, self-driven
evidence_summary: Khan's path to acting was driven by adversity rather than advantage: his father died when he was about 15 and his mother died around 1991, creating financial strain that he cited as a reason to pursue film acting. He had no family connections to entertainment and entered through college theatre at Hansraj College in Delhi. His TV debut on DD National (India's national broadcaster) coincided with the expansion of Indian television in the late 1980s. The loss of both parents and the need to support himself created urgency that propelled his early career.

name: Steven Spielberg
milestone_by_age_26: Made Amblin' (1968) at age 22, winning a studio contract as the youngest director ever signed to a long-term deal at Universal; directed the acclaimed TV film Duel (1971) at age 24.
early_history_summary: Spielberg began making amateur films as a child in Phoenix, Arizona, using an 8mm camera his father gave him. He made numerous short films as a teenager, including the feature-length Firelight at 17. After being rejected from film school, he interned at Universal Studios and made Amblin' (1968), a 26-minute short that impressed Sid Sheinberg, who signed him to a long-term directing contract.
family_context_summary: Born in Cincinnati to an electrical engineer father (who worked on early computers) and a concert pianist mother. The family moved to Phoenix, Arizona, and later to California. His father introduced him to technology and gave him his first 8mm camera. Parents divorced when Spielberg was a teenager.
parent_family_domain_summary: Spielberg's father was an electrical engineer who provided early access to technology and a camera, nurturing his filmmaking interest. His mother was a concert pianist. The family was middle-class but not connected to the film industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught filmmaking, early camera access, Hollywood proximity, obsessive practice, middle-class family
evidence_summary: Spielberg was a self-taught filmmaker who began making movies as a child, producing dozens of amateur shorts and a feature-length film by age 17. His father, an electrical engineer, gave him an 8mm camera and nurtured his technical interest. Growing up in Phoenix and then moving near Los Angeles placed him in proximity to Hollywood. His obsessive concentration on filmmaking from childhood — spending years making films with friends — built exceptional skill depth that was recognized when Sid Sheinberg at Universal saw Amblin' and signed him to the youngest long-term studio deal in history. His parents' divorce and rejection from film school created adversity that he channeled into relentless self-driven practice.

name: Mircea Lucescu
milestone_by_age_26: Made Divizia A debut at 18 (June 1964), won league championships in his first two seasons with Dinamo București, and debuted for the Romania national team at 21 (November 1966), earning 10 caps while still at Divizia B level.
early_history_summary: Lucescu began playing junior football in 1961 at a sports school in Bucharest. Coach Traian Ionescu brought him to Dinamo București, where he made his top-flight debut at 18 in June 1964. He won the championship in his first two seasons, was loaned to Stiința București for two seasons, then returned to Dinamo where he became a long-term stalwart and Romania international.
family_context_summary: Born in Bucharest, Romania, as part of a family of five children. Family financial background and parents' occupations are not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family football connections or athletic inheritance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Dinamo București, sports school, early debut, national team pipeline
evidence_summary: Lucescu was channeled into elite football through the Romanian sports school system, joining a sports school in Bucharest at 15-16 and being recruited to Dinamo București, one of Romania's top clubs, by coach Traian Ionescu. His Divizia A debut at 18 and immediate championship wins demonstrate the effectiveness of this pipeline. Family background is poorly documented; no evidence of family football connections or financial advantage was found. His national team debut at 21, while still playing at Divizia B level, underscores how the club and national team system identified and promoted talent independently of club tier.

name: Michael Haneke
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Haneke's first television film was made in 1973-74 at age 31-32, and his first feature film (The Seventh Continent) premiered in 1989 at age 47. By age 26 he was a university student and odd-job worker; no material directing milestone by 26 found.
family_context_summary: Son of German director and actor Fritz Haneke and Austrian actress Beatrix von Degenschild. Grew up in Wiener Neustadt in a theatrical family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were in the performing arts — father was a director/actor, mother was an actress — but this did not translate into an early filmmaking career; Haneke did not direct his first film until his thirties.

name: Patrick Swayze
milestone_by_age_26: Made Broadway debut in Goodtime Charley (1976) at age 24 and won the leading role of Danny Zuko in the Broadway production of Grease (1978) at age 25, which led to film and television offers.
early_history_summary: Swayze began dance training as a toddler at his mother's dance studio in Houston, also pursuing gymnastics, ice skating, and martial arts. After a football knee injury ended his athletic scholarship hopes, he toured with Disney on Parade, then moved to New York in 1972 to train at the Harkness and Joffrey Ballet schools. He became a principal dancer with the Eliot Feld Ballet Company before transitioning to Broadway.
family_context_summary: Born in Houston to Patsy Swayze, a choreographer and dance instructor who owned and operated a dance studio, and Jesse Wayne Swayze, an engineering draftsman. The family was described as humble means but deeply embedded in the arts. Swayze began training at his mother's studio as soon as he could walk.
parent_family_domain_summary: Swayze's mother was a choreographer, dance instructor, and director of the Houston Jazz Ballet Company who owned her own dance studio. She provided sustained, individualized dance training from toddler age and introduced him to ballet, making the family domain directly catalytic to his career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mother dance instructor, family studio, early ballet training, Broadway pipeline, physical versatility
evidence_summary: Swayze's early career was built on a family-domain apprenticeship: his mother Patsy Swayze was a choreographer and dance instructor who owned a studio in Houston, providing him with sustained, professional-level dance training from toddler age. This direct domain exposure gave him exceptional physical versatility across ballet, gymnastics, and martial arts. Despite humble financial means, the family studio was a de facto training facility. He moved to New York at 20 to train at elite ballet schools (Harkness, Joffrey), joining the Eliot Feld Ballet Company before transitioning to Broadway. Knee injuries repeatedly threatened his dance career, creating adversity that pushed him toward acting.

name: Manolo Blahnik
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Blahnik moved to London in 1969 at age 26-27 and designed his first shoe collection in 1971 at age 28-29. By age 26 he was studying art in Paris with no design or business milestone.
family_context_summary: Born in the Canary Islands to a Czech father (who fled Prague in the 1930s) and Spanish mother. Mother's family owned a banana plantation. He was homeschooled, then attended a Swiss boarding school and the University of Geneva.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as directly relevant to shoe design. His mother had a fondness for fine footwear made by a local shoemaker, which influenced his aesthetic, but there was no family business in design or footwear.

name: Toshio Suzuki
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Suzuki graduated from Keio University in 1972 and joined Tokuma Shoten as a magazine editor. He co-founded Animage magazine in 1978 at age 30 and co-founded Studio Ghibli in 1985 at age 36. No material producing milestone by age 26 found.
family_context_summary: Born in Nagoya, Japan. His family ran a small clothes-manufacturing business where he helped as a child. He studied literature at Keio University, graduating in 1972.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family ran a small clothes-manufacturing business, which gave Suzuki early exposure to manufacturing and pattern-making, but this was not directly related to animation or film production.
